properties.description: Lucy Dacus is an American singer-songwriter from Richmond, Virginia, celebrated for literate, deeply personal songwriting, a warm alto voice, and arrangements that build from sparse intimacy to cathartic crescendos. She released her debut album No Burden (2016) and followed with critically acclaimed Historian (2018) and Home Video (2021). Dacus is also a founding member of the supergroup boygenius with Phoebe Bridgers and Julien Baker, and she is noted for her narrative lyrics, emotional directness, and influence within modern indie and singer-songwriter circles.

Big Thief is an American four-piece indie rock/folk band formed in Brooklyn in 2015. Anchored by songwriter and singer Adrianne Lenker and guitarist Buck Meek, with Max Oleartchik on bass and James Krivchenia on drums, the band is celebrated for sparse, intimate arrangements, vulnerable storytelling and dynamic shifts between hushed folk and more urgent rock. Their acclaimed albums include Masterpiece (2016), Capacity (2017), U.F.O.F. (2019), Two Hands (2019) and Dragon New Warm Mountain I Believe in You (2022). They gained strong critical praise, steady festival presence and a devoted international indie audience.

AdriAnne Lenker is an American singer-songwriter and musician, best known as the lead vocalist and guitarist of the indie folk band Big Thief. She has also released solo albums showcasing her intimate, acoustic, and poetic songwriting style. Lenker's music is characterized by its emotional depth, delicate melodies, and raw, confessional lyrics. Her work often explores themes of nature, relationships, and personal introspection.

Julien Baker is an American singer-songwriter and guitarist from Memphis, Tennessee, known for her deeply personal and emotional songwriting, sparse arrangements, and haunting vocals. She began her music career in the early 2010s and gained critical acclaim for her introspective lyrics and minimalist style. Baker's music often explores themes of mental health, addiction, faith, and personal struggle, delivered with raw vulnerability and poetic lyricism.

Julia Jacklin is an Australian singer-songwriter and musician known for her intimate and emotionally resonant indie rock and folk music. She has gained critical acclaim for her storytelling ability, blending indie rock and folk influences with personal and introspective lyrics. Jacklin's music often explores themes of relationships, self-discovery, and vulnerability, delivered with a distinctive, emotive vocal style.

Better Oblivion Community Center is an indie rock supergroup formed in 2019 by American singer-songwriters Conor Oberst and Phoebe Bridgers. The duo combines elements of indie rock and folk to create emotionally resonant music characterized by introspective lyrics and harmonious vocals. Their self-titled debut album was released in 2019 to critical acclaim, noted for its blend of Oberst's seasoned songwriting and Bridgers' distinctive voice.

Matt Berninger is an American singer-songwriter best known as the lead vocalist and lyricist of the indie rock band The National. His distinctive baritone voice and introspective lyrics have made him a prominent figure in alternative and indie music scenes.

Suki Waterhouse is an English singer-songwriter, model, and actress who has developed a music career characterized by indie pop and alternative influences. She is known for her ethereal vocal style and introspective songwriting, blending pop sensibilities with alternative and electropop elements. Waterhouse's music often features dreamy melodies and a modern, stylish aesthetic that complements her background in fashion and acting.
